summary: A 1914 Siskiyou National Forest lookout rebuilt in 1963 after storm damage, with a WWII stint as an Aircraft Warning Service post, now rented out by the Forest Service.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab on 20-foot wood tower

access.note: available for nightly rental via Recreation.gov

visit.trail_note: reached via Forest Service roads 33/3348/5520/5520-020; cabin has no water, and as of 2026 no propane heat, stove, or lights pending repairs

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Siskiyou National Forest

events.note: Guard T.D. Land completed a shake shelter and lookout building, cost 25 cents in nails for the shelter
Activated September 29, 1942 as Aircraft Warning Service station 'George 6-3,' reporting to the Roseburg Filter Center
Columbus Day Storm (Oct 12, 1962) badly damaged the lookout house
20-foot tower with R-6 flat-roof cab constructed
newlywed couple Everett and Sue Deniston reported staffing the lookout in September 1972

evidence.supports: Bald Knob served as an AWS site in 1942-43; current R-6 structure built 1963; location in Siskiyou National Forest, Coos County
evidence.quote: Bald Knob served as an Aircraft Warning Service site in 1942-43 ... The current structure is an R-6 Flattop cabin on a 20 foot wood tower was constructed in 1963

evidence.supports: 1914 shelter built by T.D. Land, cost of nails, trail work, early fires reported
evidence.quote: A shake shelter was built on Bald Knob by the lookout at a cost of 25 cents for nails.
Bald Knob Lookout has reported 13 fires, 12 outside and 1 inside the Forest.

evidence.supports: Martha Price appointed fire lookout on Bald Knob itself in July 1917
evidence.quote: July 26, 1917: "Curry County probably has the distinction of having the first lady lookout in the state in the forest service. Miss Martha Price of Illahe has been appointed fire lookout on Bald Knob, near Illahe, has assumed charge of the station and is now on duty."

evidence.supports: AWS activation date and filter center
Columbus Day Storm damage and 1963 rebuild
evidence.quote: October 12, 1962: The Columbus Day Hurricane badly damaged the lookout house. 1963: A 20-foot tower with an R-6 flat roof cab constructed.
Everett and Sue Deniston were married in June. Two days after the wedding, they went up to the Barklow lookout in the Powers district of the Siskiyous. They are now at Bald Knob lookout.

evidence.supports: current rental status and lack of water/propane due to vandalism and storm damage
evidence.quote: Due to recent vandalism to propane tank and winter storm damage, there will be no propane heat, stove, refrigerator, and lights available until the next 2026 season.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's 'Built 1963' date refers to the current R-6 tower/cab; the original lookout structure on the site dates to 1914 per NHLR's own description and the Oregon Lookouts newspaper archive. The story treats 1914 as the first structure and 1963 as the rebuild.

notes_for_editor: Brief's location conflict (NHLR vs RIDB coordinates) was not resolved here since it doesn't affect the narrative; recreation.gov currently lists amenities as unavailable due to vandalism/storm damage, worth double-checking closer to the 2026 rental season for accuracy.
